Apologies in advance if this is a stupid question, but I have a couple of fountain pens lying around I haven't been able to write on because I haven't found any ink for fountain pens at local stores, and it seems that the kind meant for dip pens or calligraphy just won't flow. Do I have to look for fountain pen ink online or is there something I could mix with the ink I have to make it work?
How is fountain pen ink different from dip pen ink?

Avoid ink that contains iron gall. Many dipping pen inks contain metals that could clog the feed in a fountain pen.

Look for an ink that specifically says that it is made for fountain pens. Some good fountain pen ink manufacturers include, Noodlers, Pelikan, and Mont Blanc.

There are several good fountain pen dealers online. When you find an ink you like, write to the owners and ask them if it is safe for fountain pens before you buy, just to be on the safe side.

I'm a big fan of Noodlers fp inks. They manufacturer a wide variety of inks. Check out their website for details, and all the info you could want about the quality of fountain pen inks.
Thanks, I guess I'll have to look online. I just want something that flows well and doesn't cost too much.

We have some stores on the right hand side here for you to check out (depending on where you are). I will say Noodler's ink is generally good bang for buck (You get a really solid amount of ink in each bottle and it is filled to the top!). If you're in a colder area, consider getting it sooner than later because some places will not ship ink in the cold season as the ink might freeze on delivery.

EDIT: Also, some inks work better with some pens, so trying things out can be helpful

Iron Gall inks are perfectly safe for FP use. You as a user just has to practice good pen hygiene- not letting the ink sit in the pen for months without flushing, etc. IG ink used to be much more corrosive than modern IG is, there really isn't anything to worry about unless you are using homemade or REALLY vintage ink.

When it comes to ink, avoid anything marked "calligraphy" like the plague. Calligraphy ink has binders like shellac, which will gum up your feed, sometimes to the point of not being able to rescue it. India ink is another big one to avoid, usually even if it says it is "safe for fountain pens", it isn't. That's the major difference. A secondary difference is that most calligraphy inks are created from pigments. Those pigments, no matter how small, will also gum up the feed. There are just a few pigmented inks that are FP safe (Sailor nanopigment or J. Herbin 1670 series), all other FP inks are made from dyes.
